title: audit-gaps-during-sidecar-deployment-rollout-and-drift-detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a staged rollout of the audit-sidecar (0.9.2 -> 1.0.0), we observed a 12-minute window of missing audit entries for SSO token events and KMS-wrapped key rotations. The incident correlated with a simultaneous leader-election on the audit-ingest service and a sidecar config version mismatch that caused selective backpressure and dropped batches. This ticket tracks the postmortem follow-ups: short-term reconciliation, detection/alerting improvements, and long-term hardening to prevent audit gaps during rolling deployments and KMS rekey operations.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC: Pager alert - missing audit entries for auth-token.create observed on compliance dashboard (12-minute gap).
2026-03-01 09:18 UTC: On-call (Marcus) confirmed pattern: gaps align to pod restarts in audit-ingest and sidecar version mismatch.
2026-03-01 09:30 UTC: Mitigation - paused sidecar rollout, restarted audit-ingest replicas, enabled buffering fallback. Immediate ingestion resumed.
2026-03-01 10:05 UTC: Initial RCA: race between KMS rewrap job, leader-election in audit-ingest, and sidecar schema migration leading to dropped batch ACKs.
2026-03-02 14:00 UTC: Engineering postmortem review with PM, security, and compliance teams — agreed on action items and priority.
actions: A1: Implement transactional handoff for sidecar batch ACKs that tolerates leader-election (owner: Marcus Reed, due: 2026-03-18)
A2: Add Canary-level audit-sanity checks to rollout pipeline: verify continuity of audit stream across canary and baseline for 30 minutes before promoting (owner: Lina Chen, due: 2026-03-12)
A3: Emergency reconciliation job to rehydrate missing audit entries from local buffers and KVS for the affected window (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-08)
A4: Harden KMS rekey orchestration with a deployment fence to prevent concurrent rewrap + rolling updates (owner: Security Infra, due: 2026-03-20)
A5: Create an end-to-end integration test that simulates leader-election during a sidecar schema change (owner: QA, due: 2026-03-15)
A6: Update runbook for on-call to include immediate steps: pause rollout, enable buffering fallback, escalate to Security for any KMS anomalies (owner: On-call Lead, due: 2026-03-05)
A7: Add metric + alert: contiguous audit-seqgap > 5s triggers P1 on-call with trace link (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-11)
decisions: D1: Freeze current sidecar rollout channel until transactional ACKs are implemented and canary checks pass.
D2: Require KMS rewrap jobs to set a cluster-wide lock that prevents simultaneous control-plane upgrades during rewrap windows.
D3: Surface audit continuity status in Redwood Console per-org so customers can see any ingestion anomalies in near-real-time.
D4: Prioritize reconciliation job and canary checks as P0 for security/compliance customers with SLAs.
followups: F1: Engage Compliance to review reconciled audit entries and sign off on acceptability for regulated customers (owner: Compliance, due: 2026-03-25)
F2: Run a tabletop exercise simulating KMS rekey + rolling deploy to validate runbook (owner: Incident Response, due: 2026-04-02)
F3: Document lessons learned and publish a public-facing incident summary for impacted customers (owner: Communications, due: 2026-03-22)
F4: Evaluate quorum-based leader-election tuning to reduce election churn during maintenance windows (owner: Platform, due: 2026-03-30)
notes: Related to but distinct from previous KMS rotation postmortems; root cause here is interplay between sidecar schema drift + leader re-election, not KMS crypto bug.
We observed increased likelihood of sequence gaps when average batch sizes exceeded 4MB under backpressure.
Customer outreach: initial emails drafted by Comms; legal to review for regulated customers.
